title: TarDiff: Target-Oriented Diffusion Guidance for Synthetic Electronic Health Record Time Series Generation

problem.claim: Synthetic EHR time-series generation is needed to address data scarcity for clinical machine learning.

gap.claim: Distribution-focused synthetic-data methods may overrepresent common patterns and fail to improve performance on rare but important conditions.

contributions.claim: TarDiff is a target-oriented diffusion framework that incorporates task-specific influence guidance into synthetic EHR generation.
The framework quantifies expected downstream contribution with influence functions and embeds the resulting influence gradient into reverse diffusion.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe TarDiff as a novel target-oriented diffusion framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across six publicly available EHR datasets, the authors report up to 20.4% higher AUPRC and 18.4% higher AUROC than existing methods.
The authors report that TarDiff preserves temporal fidelity while improving downstream model performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Synthetic EHR time-series generation can provide additional training data for clinical machine learning.
Existing methods primarily reproduce statistical distributions and temporal dependencies, which may neglect rare important conditions.
Synthetic samples should be generated to improve the performance of specific clinical models.
TarDiff uses task-specific influence estimates and influence gradients to steer reverse diffusion toward utility-optimized samples.
The authors report strong benchmark performance, temporal fidelity, and improved downstream model performance.

source_observation.claim: Matching observed-data distributions alone may not improve downstream performance when common patterns dominate.

interpretation.claim: Synthetic-data objectives can be aligned with downstream task utility rather than fidelity alone.

application.claim: For imbalanced clinical tasks, evaluate and guide generation using task-specific performance effects.

exception.claim: Task-oriented guidance may not generalize beyond the clinical tasks, datasets, or conditions evaluated in the abstract.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six datasets, downstream tasks, baselines, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not report computational costs, ablations, or implementation details.
